key_insight: Learning across space and time makes micro-CT segmentation more reliable by distinguishing real pore and fluid changes from segmentation errors.
engineering_relevance: More consistent measurements of pore evolution and fluid displacement support analysis of geological carbon storage, underground hydrogen storage and groundwater contaminant transport.
method: Use a transformer-based 4D framework to segment sequential 3D micro-CT images.
Combine spatial and temporal information to resolve ambiguous phase assignments.
Quantify pore growth, permeability evolution and fluid-filling events without per-image parameter adjustment.
evidence_signal: Dissolution tests showed more accurate pore-volume growth and rock boundaries than an equivalent 3D model, permeability trends verified against reference segmentations and flow simulations, transfer to another sample without retraining, and reduced spurious variation on two fluid-displacement datasets.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish performance across broader rock types, imaging conditions or temporal sampling rates.
paper_title: Spatiotemporal learning improves quantification of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement
